src.image_utils module

Utilities for image processing and filtering. Centralizes image-related logic to avoid duplication.

src.image_utils.should_skip_image(img_element, src)[source]

Determine if an image should be skipped during import.

Filters out: - UI icons (JIRA, Confluence icons) - Emoticons - Bullets and decorative elements - Confluence thumbnails - GIF animations (usually UI elements)

Parameters:

  • img_element (Tag) – BeautifulSoup Tag element

  • src (str) – Image source URL

Return type:

bool

Returns:

True if image should be skipped, False if it should be imported

src.image_utils.extract_image_src(img_element)[source]

Extract and normalize image source URL from img element.

Prefers data-image-src over src (Confluence exports use data-image-src for full-size images, src for thumbnails).

Removes query parameters that can cause 404s.

Parameters:

img_element (Tag) – BeautifulSoup Tag element

Return type:

Optional[str]

Returns:

Normalized image URL, or None if no valid source

src.image_utils.is_content_image(img_element)[source]

Check if an image is actual content (not UI decoration).

Parameters:

img_element (Tag) – BeautifulSoup Tag element

Return type:

bool

Returns:

True if this is a content image that should be imported

src.image_utils.normalize_image_url(src, base_url)[source]

Convert relative image path to absolute URL using base URL.

Parameters:

  • src (str) – Image source (relative or absolute)

  • base_url (str) – Base URL for serving images (e.g., tunnel URL)

Return type:

str

Returns:

Absolute URL for the image

src.image_utils.is_table_icon(img_element, src)[source]

Check if image is likely a small icon/emoji suitable for tables.

Icons are small images that can be rendered inline in Notion tables as emojis or small decorative elements.

Parameters:

  • img_element (Tag) – BeautifulSoup Tag element

  • src (str) – Image source URL

Return type:

bool

Returns:

True if image is a small icon suitable for table cells

class src.upload_strategies.S3TempStrategy(bucket, region, access_key, secret_key, lifecycle_days=1, use_presigned=True)[source]

Bases: UploadStrategy

S3 with auto-delete lifecycle rules (RECOMMENDED).

Uploads to S3 with: - Temporary storage prefix (notion-temp/) - Lifecycle rule: auto-delete after 1 day - Pre-signed URLs (expire in 1 hour)

Pros: - Auto-deletes via S3 lifecycle rules (reliable!) - You control the infrastructure - Very reliable (99.99% uptime) - Fast CDN delivery - Cheap (~$0.001 for temp storage)

Cons: - Requires AWS account setup (15 min) - Tiny cost (~$0.001 vs free)

Best for: Production imports (100-1000+ pages)

class src.upload_strategies.NotionNativeStrategy(s3_bucket, s3_region, s3_access_key, s3_secret_key)[source]

Bases: UploadStrategy

Notion native file upload via S3 temp bridge (EXPERIMENTAL).

Uses S3TempStrategy as bridge instead of file.io (more reliable).

Approach: 1. Upload to S3 temp storage 2. Give S3 URL to Notion 3. Notion downloads and caches 4. Notion converts to ‘file’ type (hopefully) 5. S3 lifecycle auto-deletes after 1 day

Pros: Images become Notion-hosted, reliable bridge Cons: Experimental conversion, requires S3 account

  • s3_bucket (str)
